problem: What is the gradient of the product $f(x, y)g(x, y)$ if $f(x, y) = \ln x\ln y$ and $g(x, y) = x^{2}y^{2}$?

selected_existing_owned_answer.:answer/value: xy^{2}\ln y(2\ln x + 1)i + x^{2}y\ln x(2\ln y + 1)j

worked_solution:
The product is $fg=x^2y^2\ln x\ln y$, defined for $x>0$ and $y>0$. Applying the product rule separately to each variable gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
(fg)_x&=xy^2\ln y(2\ln x+1),\\
(fg)_y&=x^2y\ln x(2\ln y+1).
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore

$$
\nabla(fg)=xy^2\ln y(2\ln x+1)i+x^2y\ln x(2\ln y+1)j.
$$
